To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the water content affects the thermal transitions, molecular mobility, and mechanical properties of corn flakes.

the compression force showed maxima at water content of ca. 13% (db) in SCF and 16% in CCF, whereas the spin-spin relaxation time showed a minimum in the same water content range, and T g values determined either by spin-spin relaxation or by DSC showed a decrease with increasing water content.
the water content in corn flakes has a significant influence on the glass transition temperature and the mechanical properties of the product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the effect of water in corn flakes.
the development of an integrated approach to assess the water effect on the quality of corn flakes, by combining DSC and NMR techniques.
the analysis of the water effect on thermal transitions, and mechanical properties, as well as the molecular mobility, in corn flakes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
water content affects the mechanical properties and molecular mobility of corn flakes, but in different manners.

the maximum in compression force as a function of the water content in corn flakes is related to the water mobility and to the molecular mobility of the solid phase, but not to the glass transition temperature.
the water content of corn flakes has a profound effect on the thermal and mechanical properties, and on the molecular mobility of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
while water content has a profound effect on mechanical properties, the effect of moisture on T g values is not as significant.
the mechanical properties of CF depend on both solid and water mobility, while the latter is the main determinant of the former.
the mechanical properties of corn flakes are more sensitive to the effect of moisture than the glass transition temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the water effect on the mechanical properties and molecular mobility is more complex than the effect on the thermal transitions.
the effect of water content on thermal transitions, molecular mobility, and mechanical properties is not the same.
water content has an important role in the quality of corn flakes.
